goal: Invariant laws remain invariant under n-step kernel powers
source_anchor: Fearnhead–Nemeth–Oates–Sherlock arXiv:2407.12751v1 §1.3, printed pp.17–19 / PDF pp.23–25; Chen–Štefankovič–Vigoda arXiv:2307.13826v4 §3 mixing arguments using ν P^t
theorem_delta: For any measurable state space, kernel κ and measure μ, if κ.Invariant μ then (κ ^ n).Invariant μ for every n : ℕ; equivalently μ.bind (κ ^ n) = μ.
truth_boundary: Only finite-step propagation of an already invariant law is formalized. No uniqueness, irreducibility, aperiodicity, convergence from nonstationary starts, spectral gap or mixing rate is inferred.

goal: Recover a joint law from a marginal and conditional distribution
source_anchor: Fearnhead–Nemeth–Oates–Sherlock arXiv:2407.12751v1 §2.1.1 Component-wise updates and Gibbs moves, printed p.48 / PDF p.54; Chen–Štefankovič–Vigoda arXiv:2307.13826v4 §1.3 Glauber dynamics/Gibbs sampler
theorem_delta: For measurable spaces α and nonempty Standard-Borel β, a finite measure μ on α × β is recovered exactly by the composition-product of its first marginal and the regular conditional law of the second coordinate given the first.
truth_boundary: This cell proves only the joint-law disintegration identity. Constructing a state-to-state heat-bath kernel, proving its invariance/reversibility, choosing random or deterministic scan order, and proving ergodicity/mixing are separate downstream obligations.
